name: Land highly susceptible to landslides (USGS, %)
plain: How much of the land is in the three most landslide-prone classes of the USGS map: the places where intense rain is most likely to set off a slide.
definition: The share of the land that the USGS map of susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall (Hughes and Schulz, 2020) puts in its High, Very High or Extremely High class: the most susceptible 30% of the main island. Over all the land of the area that the map classifies, in percent.
unit: % of the land the map classifies
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (no value for Vieques and Culebra); also 901 barrios (no value for the 15 on Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona)

coverage.frequency: One model, published in 2020 (its GIS layer in 2021). The build checks the first author's copy for an edit (refresh unit landslide).

method: landslide.py reads the 7,294 PNG tiles of zoom 15 that cover the main island (4.8 m a pixel in Web Mercator, about 4.5 m on the ground), turns each pixel's color back into its class (gray Low, yellow Moderate, orange High, red Very High, blue-violet Extremely High; the build stops on any other color) and counts each pixel's ground area in the barrio whose outline holds its center (or the nearest within about 1 km, for the generalized coast). No raster library is used: the PNGs are decoded with zlib and numpy. Checks against the report, run at every build: the classes cover 40.0, 30.0, 20.0, 9.0 and 1.0% of the 8,739 km2 classified (the report: 40, 30, 20, 9 and 1% of 8,700 km2), and the 71,431 slope failures of Hurricane María fall 1.2, 10.2, 29.4, 44.4 and 14.7% in the five classes (the report's table 5: 1.2, 10.0, 29.4, 44.6 and 14.9%), so the tiles are the published map. A barrio's share is the area of the three classes over all its classified area; a municipio's and Puerto Rico's shares come from the areas of their barrios. The share of each of the five classes is a dataset of its own (landslide.ls_cls_low_pct to landslide.ls_cls_extremely_high_pct).
source_detail: Hughes and Schulz (2020), USGS Open-File Report 2020-1022; GIS layer: USGS data release https://doi.org/10.5066/P990ZP4C (5 m raster, five classes). Read from the first author's tile copy, https://tiles.arcgis.com/tiles/TQ9qkk0dURXSP7LQ/arcgis/rest/services/Susceptibilidad_Derrumbe_PR/MapServer, zoom 15. Barrio outlines: barrios.geojson; residents: 2020 census blocks (population_blocks.json).
how_to_read: Puerto Rico (the main island): 30.0%, by the map's design. Highest: Maricao (79.8%), Jayuya (70.4%), Las Marías (69.5%). 4 municipios have less than 0.5%, and 55 barrios have none; 229 barrios have half or more of their land in these classes.
caveats: A relative ranking within Puerto Rico, not a probability: the classes are set by area (the most susceptible 30% of the island is High or above), so 'high' means high compared with the rest of the island.

The map shows where landslides may start during or soon after intense rainfall; it does not show where a slide travels downhill, and deep bedrock slides and earthquake-triggered ones are poorly represented. It is not a substitute for a site-specific slope-stability study.
Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona are not in the USGS model: no value. Puerto Rico's figure is the main island's.
